front.title: Client Groups for Shared HTTP Connections

abstract.t: Intermediaries often carry requests from many unrelated clients over one HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 connection to an origin server. The origin has no way to know this, to say whether it accepts it, or to act on the traffic of one client without disturbing every other client on the connection. This document defines a pair of settings that let an intermediary and an origin agree on whether a connection is shared, a request header field that marks which client a request belongs to, and a frame that lets the origin drain, block, or limit one client on a shared connection. It also states what an intermediary needs to do so that GOAWAY and connection failures reach only the affected client streams.
